union.summary: wrappedList answers `true` in silent (paragraph-terminator) mode for empty bullets the real `list` rule will then refuse, so out-of-diff consumers of that answer cut the paragraph with nothing replacing it
union.evidence:
`isEmptyBulletLine` (packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:31-49) only checks `state.sCount[line] < state.blkIndent`. Upstream markdown-it's `list` rule additionally bails on `state.sCount[startLine] - state.blkIndent >= 4` (indented-code territory), and the wrapper at line 181-193 short-circuits before ever delegating to `originalList`, so that guard is bypassed.

The consumers of the silent answer are all outside the diff: markdown-it's own `paragraph` rule (`rules_block/paragraph.mjs`, via `getRules('paragraph')`), markdown-it's `blockquote` rule, and the copied lheading loop at packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:121. Those callers rely on the block-rule contract "silent `true` means this rule will actually consume the line". For input `- 1\n      -` (user presses Tab twice) the paragraph is terminated, then the non-silent `list` rule declines (indent 6 - blkIndent 2 = 4) and markdown-it's `code` rule claims the line instead, rendering the empty bullet as an indented code block rather than a nested item. The fix belongs on the new code (mirror the `>= 4` indent guard inside `isEmptyBulletLine`).

union.summary: getRuleFn reads markdown-it's private `__rules__` and throws at module-evaluation time, so an in-range markdown-it upgrade takes down the whole notes editor, not just the preview
union.evidence:
`getRuleFn` (packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:207-214) reaches into `md.block.ruler.__rules__`, a private field, and `throw new Error(...)` on line 212 if the shape changes. That throw happens during module evaluation of preview.ts, because `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` runs at module scope (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:48).

The blast radius is the out-of-diff import chain: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:20 imports `NotePreview`, so `initialize()` (editor.ts:117) cannot be loaded at all; packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:95 calls that `initialize`, so the entire notes route fails, not merely the #517 rendering nicety. packages/notes/package.json:63 declares `"markdown-it": "^14.1.0"`, i.e. any minor/patch release in that range is accepted (pnpm-lock.yaml:7083 currently pins 14.3.0). Suggest degrading (skip the wrap) instead of throwing at import time.

union.summary: Code changes behaviour for `*` and `+` empty bullets, but every doc and comment describing the contract says the deviation is scoped to a "lone single `-`"
union.evidence:
`isEmptyBulletLine` accepts `-`, `*` and `+` (packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:39), so `foo\n*` and `foo\n+` now also interrupt a paragraph and emit an empty `<li>` — a CommonMark deviation on top of the documented one.

Every contract description left in the tree states the narrower rule: docs/design/notes/notes.md ("a **lone single `-`** (the empty-bullet shape) is never a setext underline, and an empty bullet is allowed to interrupt a paragraph"), docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md ("makes a *lone single dash* behave as an empty bullet"), and the plugin's own module JSDoc at packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:157-172. Either narrow the marker set to `-` or update the three descriptions.

union.summary: Design note claims "ordinary setext headings still render", but single-dash setext headings (`Title\n-`) are valid CommonMark and no longer render as <h2>
union.evidence: docs/design/notes/notes.md says "Multi-dash `---` and `=` setext underlines are untouched, so ordinary setext headings still render." `Title\n-` is an ordinary, spec-valid setext H2 and is exactly what the new `isLoneDash` guard (packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:105-110) rejects, so every already-stored note using that form silently re-renders as a paragraph followed by an empty bullet list. The only regression test covers the multi-dash form (packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:182-187) and the acceptance criteria in docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md likewise only list `Heading\n---`. The summary sentence should say single-dash setext headings are deliberately given up.

union.summary: New, undocumented plugin-ordering invariant: listEmptyBulletPlugin snapshots the `list` rule at install time, so any future md.use() added after this line silently reverts #517
union.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:48 must remain the *last* `md.use()` that touches block rules. `listEmptyBulletPlugin` captures the current `list` function once, at install time, via `getRuleFn(md, 'list')` (packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:179) and then replaces both `list` and `lheading` with `Ruler.at`. A plugin added below line 48 that calls `md.block.ruler.at('list', ...)` or `.at('lheading', ...)` — the same technique detailsPlugin's neighbours already use (packages/notes/src/view/details-plugin.ts:104) — would wholesale replace the wrapper and undo the fix, and a plugin added above it that also wraps `list` would be double-wrapped. Nothing in preview.ts records this ordering requirement, and the block-rule ordering is not asserted by any test.

union.summary: `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)` omits `options`, resetting lheading's alt chain to [] — the exact pitfall the change's own lessons doc flags for `list`, guarded there but not here
union.evidence: Line 175 calls `at()` with no third argument, while line 197 carefully passes `{ alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote'] }` for `list` precisely because, per docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-lessons.md, "`Ruler.at(name, fn, options)` REPLACES the rule's `alt` chain with `options.alt || []`". Stock markdown-it 14.x registers `lheading` with no alt (pnpm-lock.yaml:7083 pins 14.3.0), so this is currently a no-op — but the other plugins in the same pipeline (packages/notes/src/view/details-plugin.ts:104, plus @vscode/markdown-it-katex at packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:39) do manipulate alt chains, and any of them gaining an lheading entry would be silently wiped. Passing `{ alt: [] }` explicitly, or a comment noting lheading has no alt upstream, would make the asymmetry with line 197 intentional. I could not verify the installed markdown-it source (node_modules is not present in the checkout).
